bug_semantics: When phpMyFAQ uses PostgreSQL through the native pgsql PHP extension, public FAQ search interpolates the unauthenticated `search` parameter into `Pgsql::search()` as `(%s) ILIKE ('%%%s%%')` after `SearchDatabase::escapeLikeWildcards()`. That helper prefixes user `%` and `_` with `|`, which only disables LIKE wildcards if the SQL also declares `ESCAPE '|'`. Native `Pgsql.php` did not: after the BIC it had no matching ESCAPE clause (PostgreSQL default escape is backslash), and after the later 4.1 merge it declared `ESCAPE '='`. In both states `|` is a literal, so attacker-supplied `%`/`_` stay active wildcards, forcing maximally broad ILIKE matches and expensive sequential scans (availability DoS). Quotes are still passed through `getDb()->escape()`, so this is not quote-breaking SQL injection. The PDO sibling `PdoPgsql.php` declares `ESCAPE '|'` and is not affected.
flaw_origin: The flawed mechanism was first written by Copilot SWE-agent commit 086c8ad58f91a8e34ea27fabd1ba9ca0b2487f42 (GitHub PR 4180 rebase onto main), which changed `escapeLikeWildcards()` and the PDO/generic LIKE clauses from backslash to `|` “to work across all databases” but left native `Pgsql.php` untouched. That file already called the shared escaper while emitting `ILIKE ('%%%s%%')` with no ESCAPE clause. At the immediate parent the escaper still used `\`, matching PostgreSQL’s default LIKE escape, so native wildcard neutralization still held. After 086c the native backend’s escaping is a no-op. Merge 8853a0fa8 later brought 4.1’s consistent `ESCAPE '='` rewrite (df54d00ce) onto main’s `|` escaper, which is the exact `'='` vs `'|'` pair in GHSA-5hx6-c293-588h / CVE-2026-76212; that merge is an aggregate overlay, not the first write. 4.1.5–4.1.7 keep matching `'='`/`'='` and do not contain this mismatch.

reasoning: CVE-2026-76212 / GHSA-jj45-w38g-gfrj is a real LIKE-wildcard injection on the native PostgreSQL search backend: escapeLikeWildcards() emits `|%`/`|_` but Pgsql.php does not declare ESCAPE '|', so user `%`/`_` remain wildcards on the unauthenticated FAQ search form. NVD status is Received; the vendor GHSA is published and not withdrawn. The report-time sink ESCAPE '=' is the post-merge form of that mismatch, not a missing-escape-from-day-one bug and not the original 24dd5d840 wildcard-protection work (which used matching backslash ESCAPE on 4.1). BIC search started from the mechanism, not from AI markers: git log -S on the pipe escaper and Pgsql ESCAPE, then parent-tree checks. 086c8ad58f91a8e34ea27fabd1ba9ca0b2487f42 is the smallest public commit that first made native Pgsql escaping a no-op by switching the shared escaper to '|' without adding ESCAPE '|' to Pgsql.php; the parent 9ad2874f52040a58ab8823c40fcc77f3ad46e7e7 still used backslash escaping, which matches PostgreSQL’s default LIKE escape on the native query that lacked an ESCAPE clause. df54d00ce is not the BIC because it wrote ESCAPE '=' together with an '=' escaper (consistent, not this bug). Merge 8853a0fa8 is not the BIC: it is a two-parent aggregate that only overlaid 4.1’s '=' clause onto main’s already-broken '|' escaper. 4.1.7 is not a patch for this mismatch (it never had '|'). The actual patch is 17b7f5b0e181c6ced34887acc5f836eec7f6d0f8 on main, which centralizes LIKE_ESCAPE_CHARACTER so both PostgreSQL backends match the escaper.
